# dsh-file-finder
A DeepSeek Harness plugin for finding workspace files without leaving DSH: search by file name or by
file content, browse the workspace when there is nothing to type, then open the result in DSH's nat
ive preview, the plugin's own viewer, or the built-in editor.
中文文档
▶ **36-second tour (English, captions):** dsh-file-finder-promo.mp4 · 中文版
## What it does
- **Browse when there is nothing to search**: with an empty query the palette lists the current work
space directory — folders first, then files — and you can walk into a folder (Enter or →), go back u
p (Backspace) or jump with the breadcrumb. Typing switches to the normal search, and clearing the qu
ery returns to the folder you were browsing. **Escape** walks back one screen at a time: from a view
er or the editor to the folder you opened it from, then up through the folders, and only then closes

the panel.
- **Search by file name**, including a path fragment such as `src/view`.
- **Search by c

ontent**, with one result row per matching line.
- **Choose where files open**: one global **Open mo
de** picks which File surface Enter uses for text — **Native preview** (DSH's right-sidebar document
preview, the default), the plugin's own **Viewer** (read-only, with syntax colours and in-file find
) or the **Editor** (saves through DSH's workspace filesystem and refuses to overwrite a file that c

hanged after it was loaded). Cmd/Ctrl+Enter always opens the other side of view/edit.
- **Media alwa
ys uses the Viewer**: images, video, audio, PDFs, HTML and Markdown open in the plugin's Viewer what
ever the Open mode is; kinds the Viewer cannot render (Office documents, archives, binaries) go to D

SH's native preview instead, with a notice when it is unavailable.
[该节后续省略]
## File system: it already uses DSH's
There is no second filesystem hidden in this plugin:
| Operation | Owner |

| Walking, reading, writing workspace files | DSH's `ctx.fs` seam (`index.js`) |
| Search and rankin

g | This plugin (DSH exposes no reusable search service) |
| Opening in the Native preview | DSH's r
ight-sidebar document preview, via `ctx.sidebarRight.openResource()` and a `dsh-resource://file/sess

ion/<sessionId>/<path>` address |
| Opening in the Viewer | This plugin's read-only surface, rendere

d inside its own overlay |
| Editing and conflict checks | This plugin's editor, over the same `ctx.

ts own overlay |
| Editing and conflict checks | This plugin's editor, over the same `ctx.fs` seam |
The plugin is deliberately **additive**: it registers nothing into DSH's own file surfaces (no docum
ent renderer, no right-sidebar tab type, no shadowing of the Files tree), so DSH updates keep applyi
ng and uninstalling the plugin leaves DSH exactly as it was. This is recorded in ADR 0001.
When the native preview is unavailable (no live Session, or a shell without the right sidebar), the
plugin falls back to the Viewer and says so.
## Shortcuts
| Action | Default keys |

| Search by file name | Cmd/Ctrl+P |
| Search by content | Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+F |
| Toggle DS Bot / clas
sic Agent mode (only with the DS Bot plugin installed) | Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+B |
The commands are registered with DSH's shortcut service so you can assign your own keys in **Setting
s → Edit shortcuts**, but they declare **no default binding**. DSH's registry throws when one comman
d's default overlaps another's, and it throws from inside the *other* plugin's `apply()`, so claimin
g Cmd+Shift+F here took the whole Web UI boot down (`Conflicting shortcut defaults: session.fork and
files.searchContent`). The VS Code keys above are served by this plugin's own keydown handler inste
les.searchContent`). The VS Code keys above are served by this plugin's own keydown handler instead.
Note that Cmd+Shift+F is DSH's own "fork session" binding; this plugin uses it for content search, s
o rebind `session.fork` in **Settings → Edit shortcuts** if you relied on it.
In the browser Web shell (not the desktop app), Cmd+Shift+B is DSH's right-sidebar toggle. With DS B
ot installed this plugin takes that key for the mode switch, so assign a different key to `files.tog
gleBotMode` in **Settings → Edit shortcuts** if you need the sidebar binding there. On the desktop a
pp the combination is free.
## DS Bot mode switch (optional)
When the DS Bot plugin (`ds-bot`) is part of the running boot, this plugin also offers **Toggle Bot
/ classic Agent mode** on Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+B, plus a matching card in **Settings → File Finder**.
DS Bot keeps its surface switch private — it exposes no client service — so the bridge does the two
things another plugin safely can: it detects `ds-bot` in the boot graph, and it drives the controls
DS Bot renders itself (the account menu's surface-switch entry to leave Bot mode, and the DS Bot ret
urn pill to come back). Nothing is patched or forked, and DS Bot's own `ds-bot:surface` preference s
ck). Nothing is patched or forked, and DS Bot's own `ds-bot:surface` preference stays authoritative.
Without DS Bot nothing is registered or shown: the command never reaches **Settings → Edit shortcuts
**, the settings card stays hidden, and Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+B is left to whatever else owns it.
## Settings
**Settings → File Finder** covers:
- Shortcut reference with one-click try buttons, including **Open file browser** (no default binding

)
- Case sensitivity
- Extra ignored directory names (with live chips)
- Name and content result lim

its (steppers)
- The global Open mode: **Native preview**, **Viewer** or **Editor** (media always op

ens in the Viewer)
- Reset to defaults; changes save automatically
## Editing
Choose a result and press Cmd/Ctrl+Enter (or set the built-in editor as the default action). Save wr
ites the full text back through the workspace filesystem and refuses to overwrite a file that change
d after it was loaded. Reload, then save again, to take the newer version. The editor is for UTF-8 t
ext under about 1 MB. Binary files and common build or dependency directories are skipped.
Escape in the viewer returns to the folder you opened the file from; the same key works while a prev
iewed HTML page has focus, because the host injects a small Escape forwarder into the served documen
wed HTML page has focus, because the host injects a small Escape forwarder into the served document.
